subject: Egress custody / permitlist handshake — finalizing allowlist & firewall evidence
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@healthnet.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Egress custody / permitlist handshake — initial ask

Hi James / HealthNet ops team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our compliance checklist and the SOC2 evidence pack your security team requested, we need to lock down the outbound (egress) requirements for your private deployment of Redwood Private. Below are the minimal items we need from HealthNet to proceed to final acceptance: 

- A permitlist (static or limited-rotation IPs) or a customer-managed outbound proxy that will permit the control plane and model runtime connections we list below.
- Confirmation of the firewall policy: allowed CIDRs, allowed FQDNs, and permitted ports (we primarily use 443).
- Proof of ability to allow mTLS to control-plane endpoints (for telemetry, config, and heartbeat).
- DNS resolution rules: HealthNet must allow resolution for our telemetry and rollout FQDNs; if you perform DNS-sinkholing or split-horizon, please provide the relevant view config.
- A short statement (one paragraph) that HealthNet can provide to auditors describing how egress custody is exercised for private endpoints (who owns IPs, rotation window, and audit log retention).

Action items for us: we will attach a proposed list of egress IPs (attached) and an evidence QA matrix for you to complete. We expect a single allowlist handshake call to finalize. If you prefer an outbound proxy approach, tell us the FQDN and any client certs you will require.

Attachments: egress-ip-proposal.csv (draft), egress-qa-matrix.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

From: James Li <james.li@healthnet.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress custody / permitlist handshake — initial ask

Naomi — thanks for the clear list. A few clarifying questions from our infra/security side before we fill the QA matrix: 

1) Rotation: we operate a strict ephemeral-NAT regime for most outbound services. Can Redwood tolerate an ephemeral pool (rotating every 24 hours) if we provide an API to fetch the current egress IPs, or do you require static/lease-bound IPs?
2) Ports/FQDNs: you mentioned 443 — do you also need non-standard ports (e.g., 8443 or 5222) for any provisioning or health checks?
3) Fingerprinting: our firewall team wants to know whether you can do SNI or TLS fingerprinting to avoid allowing broad FQDNs. Is there a canonical SNI value we can rely on?
4) Evidence: can Redwood provide a short template paragraph describing what traffic is expected outbound from the runtime (for our auditors)?

I attached the egress-ip-proposal.csv you sent with a few internal comments. I'll loop in security@acme-corp.com (our third-party assessor) once we have a proposed config.

Thanks — James

[Attachment: egress-ip-proposal.csv (csv) — annotated]

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@healthnet.io>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress custody / permitlist handshake — technical clarifications

James — quick technical answers from the runtime/infra side: 

- Static vs ephemeral: preferred = customer allows a small set of static CIDRs (two /29s ideally). If HealthNet must use ephemeral NAT, we can support that provided you agree to: (a) publish the active egress IPs to a simple HTTPS endpoint (token-protected) refreshed every 15 minutes, and (b) provide a change-notify webhook we can subscribe to for immediate rotation events. Ephemeral-only without an API is not acceptable for audit evidence.

- Ports: primary traffic is TLS over 443. We also use 8443 for optional operator endpoints (management plane) in private deployments; 5222 is not used. Please allow 443 and, if you plan to run operator tooling from your bastion, 8443.

- SNI/TLS fingerprinting: We publish a stable SNI hostname for control-plane connections: control.us.redwood-inference.com (for US region). We also offer an mTLS option — recommended for high-security customers — where the client presents a HealthNet-managed client cert and we validate it. If you enable mTLS, you can restrict to SNI + client cert for strong assurance.

- DNS requirements: Allow forward resolution for the control-plane and telemetry FQDNs (control.us.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.us.redwood-inference.com) from any internal resolver used by the runtime. If you perform egress FQDN allowlisting at the proxy layer, ensure the proxy allows CONNECT to those FQDNs; otherwise the runtime's TLS handshakes will fail.

- Evidence template (short): "Outbound traffic from HealthNet private runtimes to Redwood Inference consists of TLS-encrypted connections to a small set of control-plane FQDNs over port 443. HealthNet enforces egress custody via either a static CIDR permitlist or a tokenized ephemeral CIDR publication API and maintains logs of IP rotations and proxy transactions for 90 days." — you may edit to match internal language.

Action items (recommended):
- HealthNet provides preferred model: static CIDRs OR ephemeral API + webhook.
- If static: confirm CIDR(s) and add to egress-ip-proposal.csv.
- If ephemeral: share API host + auth method & provide an initial token for our test harness.
- Decide on mTLS requirement. If yes: exchange cert signing details (we support standard CA-signed client certs or mutual TLS via our managed CA).

I'll attach an updated egress-qa-matrix with technical columns filled.

-David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: egress-qa-matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — updated by Redwood]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@healthnet.io>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress custody / permitlist handshake — summary and next steps

Thanks everyone — good progress. Summary and next steps (HealthNet action items bolded):

1) Choose approach (static CIDR OR ephemeral API + webhook). If static, provide two /29s and confirm port 443 (+ optional 8443) by EOD 2027-10-24. **HealthNet: confirm selection and populate egress-ip-proposal.csv.**
2) mTLS: Redwood recommends mTLS for auditor-friendliness. If HealthNet will require mTLS, please indicate and we will send CSR templates and an initial test client cert. **HealthNet: confirm whether you will require client certs.**
3) Evidence paragraph: use David's suggested template and copy it into your auditor statement. If you need edits for wording or retention windows, tell us. **HealthNet: provide final one-paragraph statement for auditors.**
4) Meeting to sign off: propose 2027-10-26 11:00 PT for a 30-minute allowlist handshake call to validate IPs and test connectivity. Please confirm availability.

Attachments for convenience: egress-ip-proposal.csv (v2 with our comments), egress-qa-matrix.xlsx (final draft), safelist-statement-draft.pdf (template for your auditors).

If HealthNet prefers, we can perform a short connectivity test from a staging runtime once we have the CIDRs or API credentials — this typically takes 15 minutes and proves both DNS and mTLS behavior.

Best,
Naomi
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: safelist-statement-draft.pdf (pdf)]
